verdicts.note: The tally and the 18 s, 35 s and 35-of-37 figures reproduce. The headline does not. (1) The day-scale M2 rows measure how long the durable cursor sat idle. They are not no-progress windows. Row 12 (08-18 to 08-23, '5 days'): aiur main got 277 commits and there were 158 pr.merged wakes; the 08-23 18:30Z meta records 66 merges that day. Row 22 (11 d) overlaps row 23 (global pause, M3), and only 12 wakes arrived 08-25 to 09-01. Row 28 (13.5 d) is a mostly idle aiur daemon (5 wakes on 09-04, 1 on 09-09, 21 from 09-12 to 09-16 17:52Z) while the Executor worked on other repos, and aiur quick-fixes still merged on 09-10/11 (20 merged wakes). Row 32 (archon 'manual mode', ~10 h): ACN went from 7/13 to 9/13 merged, and the Executor wrote 'every event is being acted on out of band'. Row 37 overlaps 21 aiur merged wakes on 09-18. Row 44 (khala, 6 d) overlaps rows 41, 42, 43 and 45, and the khala daemon was down 09-20 03:20 to 09-24 18:48 (17 wakes in that span). Row 38 is a record gap, as the report admits. So the register double-counts overlapping windows, and '50 no-progress gaps' are not 50 independent stalls. (2) 'Longest gaps (days) are all M2 or M3' is false by the register itself: row 45 is M8 at 111.5 h (4.6 d). With the cursor-lag rows removed, the longest real stalls are M3 (row 23, ~8 d), M8 (4.6 d), then M5 (>=23 h, >=19.5 h), M1 (~22 h), M3? (19.6 h), M7 (~19 h), M6 (~15 h) and M4 (12.75 h). (3) M1+M4 (Executor present, attention elsewhere) is 11 rows, the same as M2. Several M2 rows are loops the Executor wrote wrongly (row 33 waiter filtered 'ci', row 40 watcher scope, row 38 prompt without the retro step), not 'no consumer'. (4) The fast-response evidence is thin. Push to wake in 18 s is daemon latency, not Executor response. 'Approve 68 s' is really 're-review posted 68 s after the worker finished', and that review opened rework cycle 6 (rework label 35 s later) rather than approving. It covers one PR at fleet 1/5, when the Executor said the #164 loop 'is the whole run'. The 35/37 figure comes from Executor-logged monitoring_outcome records over ~9 h on 08-02, before the wake inbox existed, and that run's own 11:54Z retro says wakes were under-recorded. Minor: row 1 predates the 08-02 window.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The register lists 50 dated stall rows with the stated tally (M2 11, M6 11, M3 8, M4 6, M1 5, M5 5, M7 3, M8 1). The rows overlap, and several are not no-progress windows. The day-scale M2 rows (5 d, 11 d, 13.5 d, 6 d, 3.7 d; archon 10 h) measure how long the durable cursor sat idle. In each of them, work either continued (through the tail monitor, gh polling or manual driving) or the daemon or fleet was paused or down. With those removed, the longest real stalls are: Executor absence (an unnoticed ~8-day global pause, 08-25 to 09-02); operator choice (4.6 d); human or authority gates (>=19.5-23 h, and 15-16 days for two decision-blocked PRs); serial review with the Executor present (~22 h); misdiagnosis (~19 h); and silent daemon strands (~15 h). The evidence supports 'idle windows are longest when no Executor is running or a human gate is closed'. It does not show that discovery-path loss causes the longest gaps. M1+M4 (Executor present, attention elsewhere) also has 11 rows, the same as M2. The quick-response evidence is one low-load archon PR loop: 18 s is the daemon's push-to-wake latency, and the Executor applied the rework label 35 s after a review. The other evidence is 35 of 37 Executor-logged actions over ~9 h on 08-02.

I used the notification-only tail'. Of episode 2's ~1,179 backlog at 09-02, 731 arrived 08-23 15:37-24:00Z and 380 on 08-24, while the Executor was active (63 merged wakes on 08-24). The long frozen spans line up with idle or down daemons: aiur 08-25 to 09-01 had 12 wakes; aiur 09-12 to 09-16 17:52Z had 21; the khala daemon was down 09-20 03:20 to 09-24 18:48 with 17 wakes. verdicts.corrected_claim: Every repo bypassed the durable executor-wait cursor, and the lags reproduce. aiur: cursor at 1 until 2,832 on 08-23; frozen at 2832 until 09-03 with ~1,140-1,500 pending; 4329 idle 09-03 to 09-16 with 198 pending; last ack 09-17 02:56Z, after which 66 were never acknowledged. That is 4 aiur episodes, not 5. architecture-docs: 1,529 of 1,881 never acknowledged. archon: 264 of 810. khala: stuck at 517 from 09-18 to 09-24 with ~262 pending, then drained. These are cursor-lag numbers, not counts of missed events. In most episodes the Executor received the same events through the notification tail, a Monitor or gh polling, and called the stale cursor harmless. 48-82% of the aiur episode-1/2, archon and architecture-docs backlogs are system and capacity noise. The longest frozen spans are periods when the daemon or fleet was paused or down. The data proves the Executor did not use executor-wait. It does not measure lost discovery. Costly lost discovery is documented only for 08-18 to 08-23 (no monitor) and for the khala monitor lapses on 09-24 and 09-25.

verdicts.note: Holds: two paths exist. The tail/Monitor is notification-only and cannot advance the cursor; the 09-02 handoff quote is verbatim, and the skill says 'The tail is notification-only. It does not advance the durable cursor'. Monitors do not survive a session ('re-arm on session start - none survive'). The khala e09 run used a '30-minute re-arm' Monitor. Monitors 'expired without being re-armed' on 09-25 and 'lapsed after the session resume' on 09-24. The aiur 08-23 Monitor, though, was persistent, so the 30-minute expiry is a per-session harness choice. The lease figures hold. aiur claims.json: last_acknowledged_at 09-17T02:56:40Z, last_renewed_at 09-22T15:39:28Z. archon: claimed 09-10T23:59Z, 0 acks, renewed to 09-12T12:12Z (36.2 h). The mechanism is more specific than 'renews after the consumer is dead': the renewer is the daemon's own --executor Principal, so lease liveness equals daemon uptime by design. Refuted: 'so the roster shows a healthy consumer'. Roster.derive_state marks a live lease with frozen acks and pending > 0 as `stalled`, and the architecture-docs handoff recorded exactly that state. The real gaps: the roster runs only on demand (aiur's last recorded observation is 09-16T22:03Z, before the last ack, so nobody looked after it); `status` shows only CURSOR/PENDING with no consumer state; and nothing alerts or escalates. 'PENDING grows while nobody reads it' is also inaccurate. Archon metas logged PENDING 45, 115, 139, ~168, 203 and 233 hour by hour as 'manual mode', and khala noted 89 to 155 as 'Harmless'. Executors read the number and chose to dismiss it because the tail was delivering events.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The Executor had two wake paths. The notification-only `tail -F`/Monitor delivered events but never advanced the durable cursor. It died with the Executor session; in the khala e09 run it was a 30-minute Monitor needing re-arms, and it lapsed without a re-arm on 09-24 and 09-25. Only `executor-wait` acknowledges. The owner lease in `<repo>.executor.claims.json` is claimed and renewed every ~200 s by the daemon's own `--executor` Principal (#2480, 09-02), so it tracks daemon uptime, not consumer liveness. aiur renewed until 09-22 15:39Z after its last ack at 09-17 02:56Z, and archon renewed for 36 h with 0 acks. The roster does not show a healthy consumer: `executor-roster` classifies a live lease with frozen acks and pending > 0 as `stalled`, and one handoff recorded that state. The masking is elsewhere. The roster runs only on demand and nobody ran it after aiur's last ack. `status` shows only `WAKES CURSOR/PENDING` with no consumer state. No alert or escalation fires. Executors did read the growing PENDING count but called it harmless because the tail was covering events.
